prize_parts.citation: for showing how technological change and trade exposure reshape labour demand, wage structure and local labour-market adjustment

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged from round 1: B006 with Autor, Hanson and Katz. Its justification is tighter after the exchange. The achievement is a framework for how technology and trade shift labour demand, together with design-based evidence on who bears the adjustment costs. The skill-premium line is about three decades old, the task framework over two decades, and the China-shock papers over a decade. The findings have been replicated, extended across countries and attacked on inference, and the dispute is about magnitude and persistence, not existence. The chair asked which argument moved me from B004 and whether it would survive without knowing colleagues' positions. It is the attribution argument. The shortlist itself lists eight credited names for B004, and any trio of Calvo, Taylor and Woodford writes out the estimated and empirical layer (Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets) that made the framework usable. I can check that against the shortlist and the candidate descriptions, so it does not depend on how many colleagues ranked B006 first. B006's credit problem is smaller and can be handled in the citation. On the Katz-versus-Dorn question the chair put, I keep Katz, and I hold that as a judgment, not a certainty. The citation covers how technology and trade shift labour demand and wage structure, and Katz's wage-structure and skill-premium work is the part that neither Autor nor Hanson carries alone. Dorn's claim on the China-shock papers is strong, but Autor and Hanson already carry that design in the credited set. The citation deliberately says nothing about originating the task model, and it names neither a settled long-run magnitude nor the education-race theme of the 2023 prize.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakest point. Dorn is a central co-author of the China-shock papers and is excluded only because of the three-person cap. Levy, Murnane and Acemoglu contributed to the task framework outside the credited set. Katz's best-known education-technology work was done with Goldin, so his marginal claim rests on his separate wage-structure and skill-premium contributions, and several colleagues rightly call this the closest call in the trio. Technology and trade may be two adjacent discoveries and not one. The 2023 and 2024 prizes are thematically adjacent, even if neither recognised the task framework or the import-competition evidence. The persistence of the China-shock effects and shift-share inference are still debated. A cleaner alternative exists if the committee will not accept a combined citation: Autor, Dorn and Hanson for the trade-shock design alone, or Autor and Hanson as a pair.

responses.point: Friberg ranks B006 sixth and would credit only Autor and Hanson. He reads B006 as two related lines, with Katz's education-technology work partly with Goldin sitting beside a prize given in 2023. He prefers B007 for its cleaner credit and unified framework.
responses.response: The Autor-Hanson pair is the most conservative reading of B006 and I do not think it is unreasonable. It avoids both the Katz-Goldin overlap and the Dorn exclusion question. My objection is that the pair is a trade-shock-and-task prize, and it removes the supply-and-demand account of the skill premium that gives the empirical findings their interpretation. I would accept the pair before I would accept a three-name set with a loose citation. On B007, I agree its attribution is cleaner, and I ranked it fifth, not lower. Where I differ is that the cross-country identification of constitutional and electoral effects is weaker than the design-based evidence in B006, and you list that same weakness yourself. I would say plainly that if B006 fails on credit, a narrower B006 is a better fallback than B007.

responses.point: Strömberg calls Katz's marginal claim the most exposed part of the trio because of the work with Goldin. He names Autor, Dorn and Hanson as the natural fallback within the same discovery, and asks whether one citation can hold both strands.
responses.response: I agree that Katz is the most exposed name and that Autor, Dorn and Hanson is the natural fallback. I would use it if the committee decides the citation must be a single trade-shock discovery. My answer to your one-or-two question is that one citation can hold both strands if it is framed around labour-demand adjustment, since both strands ask how exposure shifts demand and who pays. The test is whether the citation can be drafted without restating the 2023 prize. The wording I propose is 'technological change and trade exposure reshape labour demand, wage structure and local labour-market adjustment'. It does not mention education, gender or the origination of tasks. If colleagues find that drafting fails, the fault would show up exactly at Katz, and I would then move to Autor, Dorn and Hanson.

responses.point: Krusell moved from B007 to B006 on the merits. He keeps Katz over Dorn because Katz anchors the long-run technology, education and wage-structure strand, and he says the case does not rest on how many colleagues ranked B006 first. He keeps B007 as an alternative and discloses his IIES tie to Persson.
responses.response: I accept the Katz-over-Dorn reasoning and I give the same reasons. Dorn's exclusion follows from the cap and not from a weaker contribution to the China-shock papers, so it should be stated as a cost in the committee's reasoning. I would add that this logic holds only if the citation really spans both strands. If the committee narrows the citation, your argument for Katz no longer applies. I also note your disclosure on B007. I do not adjudicate it, but it is a reason to test B007 on identification and distinctness from the 2024 prize and not on opening rank, and on those criteria I still rate B006 higher.

responses.point: Teorell ranks B004 second and names its attribution as far more severe than B006's. He calls Katz-versus-Dorn the committee's closest call within B006, and he would not object to a narrower trade-shock configuration.
responses.response: We agree that B004's attribution problem is more severe, and my reversal on it rests on that point. Your reading that Acemoglu's recognition is an authorship overlap on task-model theory and not a duplicated prize is also right. It is why I would keep the citation away from origination claims. I part from you only slightly on the closest call. I do not treat it as an open one for my own vote: the combined citation is defensible, and I would rather commit to it than keep the narrower option in the configuration. If a majority judges that the two strands cannot be drafted as one, I would accept the Dorn variant, and I would say so openly.

responses.point: Enflo treats Katz as the most contestable name in her configuration and wants to see the committee's view on the Katz-Goldin overlap before settling. She argues that a prize on technology and trade needs both strands, and that wording should avoid claiming the task framework.
responses.response: I agree with the drafting principle and I propose to meet your condition directly. Katz's distinct contribution is the wage-structure and skill-premium line, which sets the supply-and-demand account that the task and trade evidence extends. The education-race book with Goldin is part of that same literature, but the citation does not need it. I cannot show from the supplied evidence that Katz's separate credit is large enough to settle the point, and I regard that as a real limit on my confidence. If the committee judges it thin, that is a reason to switch to the trade-shock set, not to keep a three-name set that rests on a name nobody defends strongly.

uncertainties: Whether Katz's separate wage-structure and skill-premium credit is large enough once the work with Goldin is set aside, or whether Autor, Dorn and Hanson is the more defensible set.
Whether one citation can describe technology and trade as a single discovery without restating the 2023 and 2024 prizes or claiming origination of the task framework.
How much the persistence and magnitude of the China-shock effects, and the shift-share inference concerns, should qualify the citation.
Whether a narrower pricing-and-policy-rule B004 citation could resolve its attribution problem, which would change my ranking.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to Autor, Hanson, Katz or Dorn is apparent from my supplied profile. My research in matching, auctions and fair allocation does not overlap with any credited name on a shortlisted ballot. I am an SSE affiliate alongside committee members Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, and I co-authored COVID policy work with SSE economists. None of those people is a credited name on a shortlisted ballot. I also disclose a possible bias: my applied work stresses implementation and policy impact, and that may incline me toward prizes with visible practical reach, such as B004 in my round-1 opening. I apply the same criteria as for every other field. These ties are disclosed and not adjudicated.
